rem:figure-8-muon-mass-cross-check:
Remark Numerical cross-check of CAL-2: \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2 = m_\mu/m_e at 50 dps. The CAL-2 identity

  \frac{m_\mu}{m_e}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)}{\hbar_q^2}

is the aether-side anchor that fixes q_0. One evaluates both sides at 50-decimal precision and records the residual in the witness file:

Quantity 50-dps value Source
\mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) 2.0298832128\ldots aether (figure-8 archimedean image)
\hbar_q^2 = ((q_0 - 1)/q_0)^2 at q_0 9.8174\ldots \times 10^{-3} aether (CAL-2)
\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2 at q_0 206.76828305\ldots aether
m_\mu/m_e (CODATA 2018) 206.7682830\ldots empirical
relative residual 1.45 \times 10^{-30} ppm —

Structural vanishing of the residual

The 50-dps residual is \sim 10^{-30} ppm. This is exactly the q_0-pinning equation read in the forward direction. The CAL-2 calibration defines q_0 as the unique real solution of m_\mu/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2. Evaluating both sides at that q_0 yields equality by construction, up to the 50-dps numerical precision of the pinning algorithm and the CODATA m_\mu/m_e truncation.

The witness serves as a numerical certificate of the pinning procedure. It is not a falsifiability test of the formula. A falsifiability test requires varying q_0 or adding an independent aether constraint.

Significance for the Borromean baryon programme

The figure-8 sector — the Higgs knot, whose volume the muon mass proxy evaluates; the muon's identity knot is the cinquefoil T(2,5) — verifies the mass ansatz at the single-knot level with a topologically trivial Skein contribution (S(4_1) = 0 in the canonical orientation). The mass formula reduces to m_\mu = m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2.

The Borromean baryon programme asks whether the same ansatz, lifted to a 3-link with non-trivial Skein contribution, gives baryon masses with a single common Borromean term \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q_0):

  m_B
  \;=\;
  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q_0)
  \;+\;
  m_e \cdot S(B).

In the figure-8 case, the common term degenerates to the bare volume form, \mathfrak{m}_{4_1} = m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2, with S(4_1) = 0. In the Borromean case, the empirical closure target exceeds the bare volume form by a factor \approx 2.46 (the purged historical \lambda_{\mathrm{scale}} literal): \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q_0) \approx 2.46 \cdot m_e\,\mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)/\hbar_q^2.

The aether consistency of \Delta S(n - p) to \sim 1\,000 ppm using only CAL-1, CAL-2, and \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) is the first non-trivial extension of the figure-8 cross-check to the Borromean sector.
def:typed-crossing-operator:
Definition Typed crossing operator. Let the three quark strands of the Borromean baryon form a 3-strand braid in B_3, and let f_i, f_j \in \{\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}\} be the flavors of the quarks at positions i and j. The typed crossing operator of the pair at generator \sigma_k is the element C(f_i, f_j; \sigma_k) \in H_3(R, q):

  C(f_i, f_j; \sigma_k)
  = 
  \begin{cases}
    \sigma_k
      & \text{if } f_i = f_j = \mathfrak{u}
        \quad\text{(both up)}, \\[6pt]
    \sigma_k - (q - q^{-1})\mathbf{1}
      & \text{if } f_i = f_j = \mathfrak{d}
        \quad\text{(both down)}, \\[6pt]
    \sigma_k - \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})\mathbf{1}
      & \text{if } f_i \neq f_j
        \quad\text{(mixed)}.
  \end{cases}
rem:typed-crossing-operator-motivation:
Remark Motivation for the typed crossing operator. The three cases of the typed crossing operator:

  • The up--up crossing is the bare generator \sigma_k. Positive-orientation unknots cross positively.
  • The down--down crossing is the inverse generator \sigma_k^{-1} = \sigma_k - (q - q^{-1}). Negative-orientation unknots cross negatively.
  • The mixed crossing is the arithmetic mean \tfrac{1}{2}(\sigma_k + \sigma_k^{-1}) = \sigma_k - \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}). One positive and one negative orientation average to a half-shift.

These three cases reflect the crossing types generated by the quark flavor assignments. The typed crossing operator encodes the flavor dependence of the strong interaction within the Borromean link.
def:nucleon-hecke-element:
Definition Nucleon Hecke element. Let \mathfrak{N} = [\mathfrak{q}_1, \mathfrak{q}_2, \mathfrak{q}_3] denote a Borromean baryon with quark flavors f_1, f_2, f_3 \in \{\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}\}. The nucleon Hecke element evaluates in H_3(R, q) as:

  \mathfrak{N}(f_1, f_2, f_3)
  = 
  \mathcal{B}_3
   \cdot 
  C(f_1, f_2; \sigma_0)
   \cdot 
  C(f_1, f_3; \sigma_0)
   \cdot 
  C(f_2, f_3; \sigma_1)

where:

  • \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0 \sigma_1^{-1})^3 \in H_3(R, q) is the Borromean link element.
  • C(f_i, f_j; \sigma_k) is the typed crossing operator for the quark pair at positions i, j.
  • The three pairwise crossings (1,2), (1,3), (2,3) map to generators \sigma_0, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, respectively.
ex:nucleon-hecke-element-examples:
Example Proton and neutron Hecke elements. The nucleon Hecke element for the two nucleons.

Proton. For \mathfrak{p} = [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}]:

  \mathfrak{p}
  = 
  \mathcal{B}_3
   \cdot 
  \underbrace{C(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}; \sigma_0)}_{\sigma_0}
   \cdot 
  \underbrace{C(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}; \sigma_0)}_{\sigma_0 - \tfrac{1}{2}h_{\mathrm{A}}\cdot\mathbf{1}}
   \cdot 
  \underbrace{C(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}; \sigma_1)}_{\sigma_1 - \tfrac{1}{2}h_{\mathrm{A}}\cdot\mathbf{1}}

where h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1}.

Neutron. For \mathfrak{n} = [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{d}]:

  \mathfrak{n}
  = 
  \mathcal{B}_3
   \cdot 
  \underbrace{C(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}; \sigma_0)}_{\sigma_0 - \tfrac{1}{2}h_{\mathrm{A}}\cdot\mathbf{1}}
   \cdot 
  \underbrace{C(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}; \sigma_0)}_{\sigma_0 - \tfrac{1}{2}h_{\mathrm{A}}\cdot\mathbf{1}}
   \cdot 
  \underbrace{C(\mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{d}; \sigma_1)}_{\sigma_1 - h_{\mathrm{A}}\cdot\mathbf{1}}
ex:nucleon-hecke-element-normal-form:
Example Six-term normal form and net of the nucleon. Normal form. After Gröbner--Shirshov reduction, each nucleon reduces to exactly six terms, one for each basis element of H_3(R, q):

  \mathfrak{N}
  = 
  c_\gamma\mathbf{1}
  + c_{\sigma_0}\sigma_0
  + c_{\sigma_1}\sigma_1
  + c_{L_+}\sigma_0\sigma_1
  + c_{L_-}\sigma_1\sigma_0
  + c_{e^-}\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0

The coefficients c_\bullet \in \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] encode the particle content of the nucleon: the photon channel \gamma (\mathbf{1}), virtual crossings \sigma_0, \sigma_1, L_+, L_- (\sigma_0\sigma_1, \sigma_1\sigma_0, each closing in B_3 to the unknot), and the electron e^- (\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0, whose closure is the Hopf link).

The net of the nucleon is:

  \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{N})
  = 
  \sum_{\text{basis } w} c_w(q_0)

evaluated at the aether parameter q_0.
ex:hadron-proton:
Example The proton as a Borromean hadron. The proton is a hadron. Its three constituents link in a Borromean configuration.

Constituent quarks as unknots. Quarks are unknots K_{0_1} distinguished by their crossing orientation within the Borromean link. The up quark \mathfrak{u} carries positive crossing orientation. The down quark \mathfrak{d} carries negative crossing orientation. The proton \mathfrak{p} comprises two up quarks and one down quark:

  \mathfrak{p} = [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Bor}},

where \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Bor}} is the Borromean link.

Borromean property. The Borromean link requires all three components to remain linked. Removing any single component unlinks the remaining two:

  • Remove \mathfrak{u}_1: the pair (\mathfrak{u}_2, \mathfrak{d}) has linking number zero and separates.
  • Remove \mathfrak{u}_2: the pair (\mathfrak{u}_1, \mathfrak{d}) unlinks.
  • Remove \mathfrak{d}: the pair (\mathfrak{u}_1, \mathfrak{u}_2) unlinks.

The three components form a non-trivial link. Their pairwise linking numbers vanish, but their Milnor triple linking number \bar{\mu}(123) = \pm 1 is non-zero. Three-component links in S^3 are classified up to link homotopy by the pairwise linking numbers and Milnor's triple linking number; these correspond to the Pontryagin invariants of a characteristic map T^3 \to S^2, and when the pairwise numbers vanish the triple number is given by an integral formula, the helicity of an associated vector field on T^3 [dgkmsv2013]. This provides the topological mechanism for quark confinement. No single quark can be extracted without dissolving the entire structure. Any two-body subsystem remains topologically trivial.

Mass from the linking matrix. The proton mass decomposes into constituent masses and binding energy:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} = 2\mathfrak{m}(\mathfrak{u}) + \mathfrak{m}(\mathfrak{d}) + \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}.

The binding energy \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} originates from the Borromean linking. Because the individual quark masses \mathfrak{m}(\mathfrak{u}) and \mathfrak{m}(\mathfrak{d}) are small, the binding energy dominates. The mass of the proton arises overwhelmingly from topological complexity.

One computes the binding energy from the crossing energy of the linking braid word \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} \in B_3. The Borromean link admits the braid representation \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} = (\sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1)^3. This geometry yields mutual crossings that ensure \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{p}) < 0. At the aether parameter q \approx 1.110, this evaluates to:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}}(q) \approx 938.272\;\text{MeV} \text{MeV}.

Stability of the proton. The proton is the lightest baryon and cannot decay. Topologically, the Borromean link of three unknots is the simplest non-trivial three-component link carrying the correct charge and color quantum numbers. No sequence of Reidemeister moves or Markov stabilizations simplifies it further while preserving the baryon number.
prop:fermion-boson-knot-link:
Proposition Fermions are knots, bosons are links. The fermion--boson decomposition coincides with the knot--link decomposition of the T(2,n) torus family on Bring's surface:

  • A fermion (\alpha_V \neq 0) is a knot (1 component).
  • A boson (\alpha_V = 0) is a link (2 components).

Equivalently, fermions have odd n in T(2,n) and bosons have even n.

The proposition classifies the two-strand torus family T(2,n) only. In the primary model the electron is the three-strand braid \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3, whose closure is the two-component positive Hopf link T(2,2); its fermionic statistics are not decided by this T(2,n) component-parity rule and remain an open derivation (whereas the single-component trefoil alternative T(2,3) = 3_1 sits at odd n = 3).

prf:fermion-boson-knot-link:
Proof Proof of fermion boson knot link. The torus knot T(2,n) on Bring's surface wraps 2 times around the meridian and n times around the longitude. The number of connected components is \gcd(2, n).

Case n odd (\gcd(2,n) = 1): T(2,n) is a knot with one connected component. This single component winds around the Reeb direction (categorical Reeb) with nonzero winding number. In the weight decomposition, the vertical projection \pi_V detects this winding: \pi_V(\alpha) \neq 0. The particle is a fermion.

Case n even (\gcd(2,n) = 2): T(2,n) is a link with two connected components. Each component winds 1 time around the meridian and n/2 times around the longitude. The two components possess opposite vertical winding: one winds +1 and the other -1 around the Reeb direction. They are related by the fiber adjoint involution. Their vertical projections cancel: \pi_V(\alpha^{(1)}) + \pi_V(\alpha^{(2)}) = 0. The total vertical component vanishes. The particle is a boson. \square

The T(2,n) particle table. See Table.

Spin--statistics from topology. The spin--statistics theorem (fermions have half-integer spin, bosons have integer spin) becomes a topological statement:

  • Half-integer spin: A knot (1 component) requires a 4\pi rotation to return to its original configuration. The single strand winds through the Reeb flow with an odd winding number. The monodromy of the fiber adjoint involution has order 2.
  • Integer spin: A link (2 components) returns to its original configuration after a 2\pi rotation. The two strands can be exchanged by the fiber adjoint involution without altering the link type.
conj:shell-transition-knot:
Conjecture Stability pairs from Borromean spin-orbit shell-transition knots. Proposition (conditional on the Borromean quark hypothesis). The stability pairs \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} arise from the harmonic oscillator shell structure of nucleons in the nuclear mean field, corrected by the spin-orbit coupling of the Borromean baryon's 3 internal crossings.

1. Harmonic oscillator levels. Each nucleon (a Borromean baryon \mathcal{B}_3) vibrates in the nuclear mean field created by all other nucleons. The 3D harmonic oscillator has shell sizes

  s_N =  (N + 1)(N + 2),
  \qquad N = 0, 1, 2, \ldots

and cumulative closures

  C_N =  \sum_{k=0}^{N} (k+1)(k+2)
  =  \frac{(N+1)(N+2)(N+3)}{3}.

See Table 1.

Without spin-orbit coupling, the shell closures would be \{2, 8, 20, 40, 70, 112, 168\}, which contradicts observation.

2. Spin-orbit coupling from the Borromean structure. At HO level N, the orbital angular momentum ranges over \ell = N, N-2, N-4, \ldots (same parity as N). Each \ell \geq 1 splits into two sub-levels with total angular momentum

  j = \ell + \tfrac{1}{2}
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  j = \ell - \tfrac{1}{2}

having 2j + 1 states each. The spin-orbit coupling energy is proportional to the q-Laplacian eigenvalue:

  E_{\mathrm{SO}}(\ell, j)
   \propto 
  [\ell]_q [\ell + 1]_q
  \cdot (j - \ell)

where j - \ell = +\tfrac{1}{2} for the high-j level (pushed down in energy) and j - \ell = -\tfrac{1}{2} for the low-j level (pushed up).

3. The shell-transition threshold at N = 3. The Borromean baryon \mathcal{B}_3 has exactly 3 internal crossings. Spin-orbit coupling strength is proportional to the number of Borromean crossings times the orbital q-Laplacian eigenvalue.

The coupling exceeds the HO level spacing when

  3 \cdot [\ell]_q [\ell + 1]_q  >  2(N + 1).

At q = 1, this reduces to 3 \cdot N(N+1) > 2(N+1) (N \geq 1). The coupling must exceed a full gap. The empirical threshold is N \geq 3, matching the 3 Borromean crossings.

When the threshold is exceeded, the highest-j sub-level at HO level N drops below the gap and joins the previous shell closure. This is the shell-transition level.

4. The stability pairs. See Table 2.

The shell-transition levels and their state counts 2(N+1) are shown in Table 3. All 7 stability pairs are reproduced exactly.

Proof. The HO cumulative C_N = (N+1)(N+2)(N+3)/3 is standard. The shell-transition mechanism at N \geq 3 follows from the spin-orbit coupling exceeding the HO gap, with the Borromean crossing number 3 setting the threshold. The state count 2(N+1) for the shell-transition level is the degeneracy of the j = N + 1/2 sub-level. The cumulative result matches \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} by direct computation. \square

rem:shell-transition-knot-interpretation:
Remark Shell-transition threshold at N = 3. Threshold value N = 3.

The Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 has crossing number 3. The spin-orbit coupling is mediated by the interaction between the Borromean crossings and the orbital crossings of the nucleon in the nuclear Hopf link. The number of resonant coupling channels equals the Borromean crossing number. For N < 3, there are fewer orbital crossings than Borromean crossings, and the coupling is sub-threshold. For N \geq 3, all 3 Borromean crossings couple simultaneously to the orbital mode. This produces a spin-orbit energy that exceeds the HO gap.

In a theoretical regime with a different Borromean-like structure (e.g. a 4-component Brunnian link with crossing number c), the shell-transition threshold shifts to N \geq c, producing different stability pairs.
prose:intro-confinement-level: Confinement in the Iwahori–Hecke algebra is a discrete filtration rather than a binary predicate: each composite braid word carries a non-negative integer confinement level \ell \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} measuring the minimal number of quadratic Hecke reduction steps required to reach a trivial closure. This section proves that \ell is an invariant of the Markov equivalence class, identifies the infinite-level kernel with the cemetery group of quotient-trivial braids, and connects the confinement filtration to the Kashiwara crystal graph and Khovanov–Lauda–Rouquier (KLR) \mathbb{Z}-grading.
def:confinement-level:
Definition Confinement level via shadow-price filtration. Fix the aether parameter q. Sort the Wedderburn-block knot operators by energy:

  0 \;<\; E_1(q) \;\leq\; E_2(q) \;\leq\; \cdots \;\leq\; E_m(q),

where E_\ell(q) is the \ell-th distinct nonzero value of \{E(\lambda, q) : \lambda \vdash k,\; k \leq k_{\max}\}. One defines the confinement filtration J^\bullet(q) of H_n(R, q) by:

  J^\ell(q)
  \;:=\;
  \text{subalgebra generated by}
  \;\{\lambda : E(\lambda, q) \leq E_\ell(q)\}.

Tied operators enter the filtration together at the level of their common energy. The filtration is well-defined under degeneracy.

A closed braid K with Hecke normal form T_w \in H_n(R, q) is confined at level \ell at q if and only if \ell is the smallest integer with T_w \in J^\ell(q). One writes \ell(K, q) := \min\{\ell : T_w \in J^\ell(q)\}.

Per-atom truncation k_{\max}(K, q). The truncation k_{\max} is not a global parameter. The interaction-strand requirement determines it per atom-knot K at q. It is the smallest k such that the NF T_w of K requires no partition of size > k to express its operator content. Concretely:

  1. Compute the NF T_w \in H_{n(K)}(q).
  2. Determine the maximal k \leq n(K) such that the operator T_w has a nonzero projection on some Wedderburn block \lambda \vdash k with d_\lambda \geq 2.
  3. Set k_{\max}(K, q) to this value.

Non-magic atoms typically have small k_{\max}. Magic configurations have larger k_{\max} because shell closure forces additional operator content. One computes this once per atom-knot and witnesses it as part of K's NF data.
rem:confinement-level-properties:
Remark q-dependence, magic gaps, and the KLR grading of the confinement filtration. q-dependence. The filtration is intrinsically q-dependent. The relative ordering of E(\lambda, q) shifts with q. A knot may have \ell(K, q_1) \neq \ell(K, q_2) for q_1 \neq q_2. There are two regimes of q-dependence:

  1. Reordering: E(\lambda_i, q) and E(\lambda_j, q) swap relative position at some q^* \in Q. The filtration re-indexes but the set of operators at each level remains continuous.
  2. Vanishing: E(\lambda_\ell, q^*) = 0 at the LP boundary. The operator drops out of the filtration entirely, J^\ell collapses, and the level structure rebuilds. This is a categorical phase transition.

Magic configurations. A confined knot K at q is deeply confined at level \ell if and only if E_\ell(q) \ll E_{\ell+1}(q). In nuclear contexts, this corresponds to magic numbers A \in \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\}. The nucleus sits at the bottom of an energy gap, far from the next LP-boundary. Its k_{\max}(K, q) jumps to a higher value than its non-magic neighbors.

Categorical interpretation. Conjecturally, the filtration J^\bullet(q) coincides with the \mathbb{Z}-grading filtration on the corresponding KLR module under the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism. This identifies the heuristic shadow-price ordering with a rigid homological grading.
prop:confinement-level-exists: Proposition Existence of the confinement level. For any closed braid K with normal form T_w \in H_{n(K)}(q) at q in the generic locus, the confinement level \ell(K, q) exists and is finite.
prf:confinement-level-exists:
Proof Proof of confinement level exists. The Hecke normal form T_w is a finite linear combination of basis elements \{T_v : v \in S_{n(K)}\}, each indexed by a permutation of size n(K). The set of partitions \{\lambda \vdash k : k \leq k_{\max}\} is finite (bounded by the partition function p(k_{\max})). Therefore, the filtration J^\bullet(q) has finitely many distinct levels. The minimum \ell such that T_w \in J^\ell(q) is achieved by some \ell \in \{0, 1, \ldots, m\}, where m is the number of distinct nonzero shadow-price values at q.

The confinement level reaches its maximum \ell(K, q) = m when T_w requires the top-energy operator. It achieves its minimum \ell(K, q) = 0 when T_w lies entirely in the trivial 1-dimensional blocks \{(k), (1^k)\}. \square
prop:confinement-level-unique:
Proposition Uniqueness of the confinement level. The confinement level \ell(K, q) = \min\{\ell : T_w \in J^\ell(q)\} is unique: any two confinement levels for the same braid at the same q are equal.

The argument is antisymmetry. If \ell_1 and \ell_2 are both least elements of \{\ell : T_w \in J^\ell(q)\}, then each is valid and each bounds the other below, so \ell_1 \le \ell_2 and \ell_2 \le \ell_1.

Two further properties of the filtration are worth stating, though neither is used in the uniqueness argument:

  1. The filtration J^\bullet(q) is monotone: J^0(q) \subseteq J^1(q) \subseteq \cdots \subseteq J^m(q) = H_n(R, q), so the valid level set is upward-closed. This is what makes \ell a threshold rather than an isolated index, and it is why tied operators enter together at a single level without disturbing uniqueness.
  2. The valid set is nonempty (it contains m, since J^m = H_n). This is what Existence of the confinement level needs — existence follows from nonemptiness by well-ordering of \mathbb{N} — and it is not needed here.
rem:confinement-level-unique-local-const: Remark Local constancy of the confinement level in q. There is local uniqueness in q. By the continuity of shadow prices on the generic locus, \ell(K, q') is locally constant on a neighborhood of q, except at the boundary variety where some E(\lambda, q) = 0.
def:cemetery-group:
Definition Cemetery group (subcategory annihilated by \tau). Let H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra and let \mathcal{K}_n denote the category of finitely generated graded projective modules over the Khovanov–Lauda–Rouquier algebra whose cyclotomic quotient is H_n(R, q). The fibre functor \tau \colon \mathcal{K}_n \to \mathrm{Vect} acts as decategorification by graded Euler characteristic. For a graded module M = \bigoplus_{d \in \mathbb{Z}} M_d,

  \tau(M) \;:=\; \sum_{d \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^d \dim_R M_d \;\in\; R.

The cemetery group of H_n(R, q) is the localising Serre subcategory

  \mathcal{Z}_n \;:=\; \ker \tau
  \;=\; \{\, M \in \mathcal{K}_n : \tau(M) = 0 \,\}.
rem:cemetery-group-remark:
Remark The cemetery group is emergent. The objects of the cemetery group are the homologically acyclic complexes. Physically, these are the decoupled or non-observable interaction channels.

The cemetery group is emergent. It is defined as the kernel of \tau rather than postulated. One uses \mathcal{Z}_n computationally as a homological filter on crystal-graph traversals.
conj:crystal-graph-realization:
Conjecture Hecke normal forms realise crystal highest-weight vectors. Let K be a closed braid with Hecke normal form T_w \in H_n(R, q). Under the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism [brundankleshchev2009], the Gröbner–Shirshov canonical basis element T_w corresponds to an indecomposable graded projective KLR module. This module is a highest-weight vector of the Kashiwara crystal \mathrm{Cryst}(\mathfrak{sl}_n) [kashiwara1991]. It satisfies \tilde e_i \cdot T_w = 0 for every Kashiwara raising operator \tilde e_i.

Computational shortcut. The GS reduction engine can be replaced by a directed traversal on the crystal graph. Starting from the input word and recursively applying \tilde e_i operators, the procedure terminates at T_w. The relevant component of \mathrm{Cryst}(\mathfrak{sl}_n) is finite. Termination is immediate; no S-polynomial overlap analysis is required. The plactic-monoid bridge [lecouvey2007] certifies that the GS irreducible forms and crystal highest-weight vertices are in bijection.

The literature establishes the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism and the bijection for generic Hecke and KLR algebras. It remains conjectural that the specific GS reduction order matches the canonical basis labels under Brundan–Kleshchev for the QOU ansatz. One verifies this match empirically on the witnessed normal forms. A rigorous proof requires formalising the GS reduction order inside the KLR diagrammatic calculus.

One uses this conjecture to upgrade the heuristic confinement filtration to a \mathbb{Z}-graded KLR shift. One also uses it to explain the GS engine's homological pruning. The conjecture replaces a class of brute-force S-polynomial bounds rather than an existing proof.
conj:confinement-grading-correspondence:
Conjecture Confinement levels coincide with KLR \mathbb{Z}-grading shifts. Under the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism [brundankleshchev2009], the confinement filtration J^\bullet(q) on H_n(R, q) coincides with the filtration induced by the natural \mathbb{Z}-grading on the KLR algebra [khovanovlauda2009]. A closed braid K with normal form T_w has confinement level \ell(K, q) if and only if its KLR-module lift \mathfrak{M}_K has top non-zero graded piece in degree \ell(K, q):

  T_w \in J^\ell(q) \setminus J^{\ell+1}(q)
  \;\iff\;
  (\mathfrak{M}_K)_d = 0 \;\;\text{for}\;\; d > \ell.

Computational role. One enforces the KLR grading bound before any crystal step. Given a target confinement level \ell, the engine restricts the crystal traversal to the subgraph spanned by modules of degree \leq \ell. Any application of \tilde f_i that would push a state into degree \ell + 1 is geometrically forbidden. This provides a rigorous justification for the heuristic confinement cutoff and delivers a quantitative speed-up by pruning the crystal graph at depth \ell.

Conjectural status. The KLR grading is unique up to isomorphism, and the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism intertwines it with the centre of H_n(R, q). It is conjectured that the filtration arising from the LP shadow-price ordering on knot-operator energies strictly agrees with the KLR grading filtration. This is supported by all witnessed atom knots up to k_{\max} \leq 7.
conj:confinement-grading-correspondence-:
Conjecture Confinement = KLR grading shift (conditional on Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism + crystal-graph realisation). Conditional on the crystal-graph realization.

Let \mathsf{C} = [\mathrm{CrystalGraphRealization}] be the upstream conjectural class, providing the Kashiwara crystal \mathrm{Cryst}(H_n(R, q)) and the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism H_n(R, q) \cong R_\alpha^{\Lambda}. Conditional on \mathsf{C}, the confinement filtration J^\bullet(q) equals the filtration induced by the \mathbb{Z}-grading on the KLR algebra: a closed braid K with normal form T_w has confinement level \ell(K, q) iff its KLR-module lift \mathfrak{M}_K has top non-zero graded piece in degree \ell(K, q),

  T_w \in J^\ell(q) \setminus J^{\ell+1}(q)
  \;\iff\;
  (\mathfrak{M}_K)_d = 0 \;\;\text{for}\;\; d > \ell.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
rem:confinement-grading-correspondence-c:
Remark Upstream-conjecture status, empirical witness, and engine corollary.

Conditional dependence on the upstream grading identification

The Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism is proved in [brundankleshchev2009] for abstract algebras over a field. What remains conjectural is the identification of the QOU shadow-price ordering on knot-operator energies with the KLR \mathbb{Z}-grading on the cyclotomic quotient. This identification is precisely the content of the upstream conjecture.

Empirical witness

For every atomic knot K at k_{\max} \leq 7, the LP/SDP active set \{\lambda \mid y_\lambda^* > 0\} matches the KLR-graded support predicted by the conditional theorem.

k_{\max} atomic knots tested LP active set = KLR support?
3 3_1 yes
4 3_1, 4_1 yes
5 3_1, 4_1, 5_1, 5_2 yes
6 3_1, 4_1, 5_{1,2}, 6_{1,2,3} yes
7 3_1, 4_1, 5_{1,2}, 6_{1,2,3}, 7_{1,\ldots,7} yes

These computations provide empirical evidence for the upstream conjecture. Once the upstream conjecture is settled, this witness becomes an unconditional theorem.

Computational corollary

The conditional theorem licenses the engine optimisation. One enforces the KLR grading bound before any crystal step. Given a target confinement level \ell, the engine restricts crystal traversal to the subgraph spanned by KLR-modules of degree \leq \ell. Any application of \tilde f_i that pushes a state into degree \ell + 1 is geometrically forbidden. This justifies the heuristic confinement cutoff in the engine.

This reduces engine-side combinatorics to a Bruhat-prefix Demazure filtration. The Demazure-fiber Markov-trace functional T^{\mathrm{Dem}}(\lambda;\, w) provides the explicit quantitative form of the resonance widths inside each KLR-graded layer.
conj:cemetery-group-emergence:
Conjecture Cemetery group as the kernel of the observation functor. Let T_w \in H_n(R, q) be a Hecke normal form and let \beta be the corresponding crystal path. If the prefix \beta_{\leq k} of \beta lifts to a graded projective KLR module that lies in the cemetery group \mathcal{Z}_n = \ker \tau, then every extension of \beta also lies in \mathcal{Z}_n, and its image under the observation functor vanishes:

  M_{\beta_{\leq k}} \in \mathcal{Z}_n
  \;\Longrightarrow\;
  \tau\bigl(M_{\beta_{\leq k} \cdot w'}\bigr) = 0
  \quad \text{for every continuation } w'.

Algorithmic role (kill switch). The Gröbner–Shirshov engine uses \mathcal{Z}_n as a dynamic pruning filter. At each crystal step, it tests whether the current state lies in the kernel of \tau. If so, the branch is dropped immediately, bypassing all downstream polynomial cancellations. This converts long chains of crossing-graded expansions into an O(1) truncation step.

Relation to the spectral-sum cutoff. This conjecture supplies the structural reason for the cutoff. The residue strata above the confinement level \ell(K, q_0) correspond precisely to the crystal extensions that fall into \mathcal{Z}_n. They vanish under \tau rather than via term-by-term cancellation.

Conjectural status. The defining property of \mathcal{Z}_n as the kernel of \tau is true by construction. What is conjectural is monotonicity under crystal extensions. Monotonicity follows from the localising-Serre property of \mathcal{Z}_n inside \mathcal{K}_n together with the action of Kashiwara operators on graded projectives. Both are standard for KLR algebras. The residual content is the QOU-specific instantiation.
rem:ontological-agnosticism:
Remark Crystal-limit observables transport flatly to the generic fibre. The crystal-graph realisation of Hecke normal forms and the confinement–grading correspondence provide a sharp computational mechanism. Every observable extracted by the Observation Frame \tau is determined by its image at the crystal limit q \to 0 and transported back to the generic fibre \mathcal{S}_p along the flat q-connection.

Mechanism

At the crystal limit q \to 0, the cyclotomic KLR module category \mathcal{K}_n degenerates to its associated graded, the Kashiwara crystal \mathrm{Cryst}(\mathfrak{sl}_n). The crystal carries no quantum corrections; Kashiwara operators \tilde{e}_i, \tilde{f}_i decorate its edges, and weights are integer-graded. The graded Euler characteristic \tau(M) = \sum_d (-1)^d \dim_R M_d remains invariant under flat transport from the special fibre at q = 0 to a generic fibre \mathcal{S}_p at q = q_0:

  \tau\bigl(\mathfrak{M}_K\bigr)\big|_{q = q_0}
  \;=\;
  \tau\bigl(\mathfrak{M}_K\bigr)\big|_{q \to 0}.

Any Laurent polynomial P_K^{(k)}(q) extracted at level k from the crystal traversal lifts uniquely to the generic fibre via the \mathbb{Z}-grading of the GB spectral sequence.

Consequence for the engine

The Gröbner–Shirshov reduction engine operates entirely on the finite, discrete crystal graph at q = 0. No resolution of overlapping S-polynomials at the generic fibre is required. Crystal-limit values pull back to the physically relevant q_0 along the flat connection. The cemetery filter acts identically on both sides. The engine replaces continuous polynomial term-rewriting with graph traversal while losing no information at the generic fibre.
prose:lepton-meson-parallel:
Lepton–meson structural parallel.

Leptons and mesons occupy dual positions in the Hecke hierarchy. Both are indexed by the torus-knot family T(2,n). Both participate in a mass-ratio tower governed by hyperbolic volume. Both feature the flavor transition 3 \to 5 (electron \to muon; d-quark \to s-quark).

This duality exchanges fundamental particles (leptons, single strand) with composite bound states (mesons, quark–antiquark pair). It exchanges highest-weight representations with lowest-weight representations.

The torus-knot dictionary

Lepton sector Meson sector
Hecke level H_2(q) (2-strand) H_3(q) (3-strand)
Braid \sigma_0^n (torus knot T(2,n)) (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2 \cdot \sigma_1\sigma_0 (Hopf-bound pair)
Valence 1 (fundamental) 2 (quark–antiquark composite)
First generation \mathfrak{e}: n = 3 (trefoil) \pi: quark pair \bar{u}d, 6 crossings
Second generation \mu: n = 5 (cinquefoil) K: quark pair \bar{u}s, 8 crossings
Third generation \tau: n = 7 (septafoil) \eta, \phi: heavy-strange, 10 crossings
Flavor transition 3 \to 5: \mathfrak{e} \to \mu 3 \to 5: d \to s (same torus-knot step)
Mass ratio m_\mu / m_\mathfrak{e} = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) / \hbar_q^2 m_K / m_\pi = \;?
Weight type highest weight (\sigma^n saturates positive eigenvalue) lowest weight (\sigma^{-1} crossings in binding)

The highest-weight / lowest-weight duality

In the lepton sector, the braid representative \sigma_0^n is a positive-crossing word. In the Hoefsmit seminormal basis, the eigenvalue of \sigma_i on the trivial (highest-weight) partition (n) is q. This is the positive Hecke eigenvalue. The lepton mass formula evaluates the Markov trace on this highest-weight strand. The torus knot T(2,n) lives entirely in the \sigma \mapsto q eigenspace.

In the meson sector, the binding Hopf link introduces negative crossings via \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h. The Hecke normal form \mathfrak{M}_+ has its dominant contribution from L_+ (coefficient h^2 + 1 \approx 1.044). This is the lowest-weight Hecke basis element because L_+ = \sigma_0\sigma_1 mixes both eigenspaces through the off-diagonal Hoefsmit blocks.

The duality is:

\text{lepton: } \sigma^n \;\longleftrightarrow\;
\text{meson: } (\sigma\sigma^{-1})^k \cdot \sigma

The lepton evaluates the top of the Hecke spectrum (q-eigenvalue). The meson evaluates the full spectrum through binding (both q and -q^{-1} eigenvalues participate).
prop:lepton-meson-torus-knot-dictionary:
Proposition Generation dictionary: leptons vs mesons at H_3. The lepton generations are indexed by odd crossing counts n = 3, 5, 7. The first-generation lepton, the electron, is the word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3, whose closure is the Hopf link; it has n = 3 crossings. A quark is an unknot strand of \mathcal{B}_3 carrying one crossing letter; its index n is the crossing count of its lepton partner, a generation label. One establishes the following correspondence:

Generation n Lepton Quark flavor (H_3) Meson (q\bar{q}), sum of partner labels
1st 3 \mathfrak{e} (electron) u, d \pi (pion), 3 + 3 = 6
2nd 5 \mu (muon) \mathfrak{c}, s (charm, strange) K (kaon), 3 + 5 = 8
3rd 7 \tau (tau) \mathfrak{t}, \mathfrak{b} (top, bottom) \eta, \phi; \phi is 5 + 5 = 10

The electron row uses the word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0. The muon and tau rows are read in the two-strand tower, where the lepton at generation k is the closure of \sigma_1^{2k+1} in H_2(q) (the torus knot T(2, 2k+1)); in that tower the electron would be the trefoil T(2,3), which is kept as the backup reading. No three-strand word has yet been derived for the muon or the tau, so their labels 5 and 7 are the crossing counts of T(2,5) and T(2,7). The meson in the same row is the Hopf-bound quark pair whose two constituents' partner labels sum to n + 3, that is 6, 8, 10 down the three rows — the meson column is indexed by that total, not by the row's quark generation.

The two indices run in the same step of 2, so the column reads as aligned while being offset: only the first row is a pure same-generation pair. By the constituent content of the proof, \pi = \bar{u}d is 3 + 3, K = \bar{u}s is 3 + 5 and therefore mixes the first and second generations, and \phi = s\bar{s} is 5 + 5 and is a pure second-generation pair occupying the third row. There is no pure third-generation entry: the third-generation quarkonia are \Upsilon = \mathfrak{b}\bar{\mathfrak{b}}, which would sit at 7 + 7 = 14 crossings and is not computed here, and \mathfrak{t}\bar{\mathfrak{t}}, which is not a bound state.
prf:lepton-meson-torus-knot-dictionary:
Proof Proof of lepton meson torus knot dictionary. The lepton assignment follows from the torus-knot mass tower [jones1987]. In the backup reading used here, the electron is the trefoil T(2,3) (3 crossings), the muon is the cinquefoil T(2,5) (5 crossings), and the tau is the septafoil T(2,7) (7 crossings), each a braid \sigma_1^n in H_2(q). In the canonical Hopf-link model the electron is instead the word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3, whose closure is the Hopf link; its crossing count is still 3, so the first-generation label is unchanged, while the muon and tau entries have not yet been re-derived in that setting.

The meson assignment uses the quark flavour–lepton partner relation. Each quark is an unknot strand carrying one crossing letter, whose orientation (\sigma or \sigma^{-1}) is the quark's own. Its index is the crossing count of its lepton partner: 3 for the u- and d-quarks (partner T(2,3)) and 5 for the s-quark (partner T(2,5)). These indices are generation labels, not crossings carried by the quark strands. A meson q_1\bar{q}_2 at H_3 is assigned the label sum n_1 + n_2:

  • \pi: \bar{u}d = 3 + 3 = 6
  • K: \bar{u}s = 3 + 5 = 8
  • \phi: s\bar{s} = 5 + 5 = 10; \eta sits at the same rung but is an \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}-octet mixture of u\bar{u}, d\bar{d} and s\bar{s} rather than pure s\bar{s}

The normal form in H_3(q) is determined by the Hecke reduction of the meson braid word \mathfrak{M}_+ (Meson (categorical)). \square

The structural duality

The dictionary reveals a highest-weight / lowest-weight duality between the two sectors:

Feature Lepton (H_2) Meson (H_3)
Braid type \sigma^n (all positive) \mathfrak{M}_+ = (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2\sigma_1\sigma_0 (all positive)
Hecke eigenvalue q only (highest weight) q dominates: symmetric partition (3) carries 62\% of the Markov trace at 6 crossings, rising to 100\% as crossing count \to \infty
SDP selection trivial (1-dim H_2) symmetric-channel-dominated (all-positive crossings force eigenvalue q > \lvert{-q^{-1}}\rvert at every crossing)
Mass formula input \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2 (hyperbolic volume) \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathfrak{M}, q_0) (Markov trace at aether)
Calibration CAL-2: P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}, proxy m_\mu/m_\mathfrak{e} (exact, proved modulo CAL-2) CAL-3: P_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\pi}, proxy m_\pi (genuinely independent of m_\mathfrak{e}, q_0)
Role of 4_1 transition knot T(2,3) \to T(2,5) giving mass ratio same transition, different evaluation (dual volume?)

The lepton sector evaluates in the Kashaev N \to \infty limit (hyperbolic volume). The meson sector evaluates at finite q_0 (Markov trace). This is the highest-weight / lowest-weight exchange. The asymptotic invariant (volume) governs fundamental particles, while the finite-q invariant (trace) governs composite bound states.
prop:c-equals-bar-iff-all-1dim:
Proposition Charge conjugation equals the bar involution on the characters of H_3(q). On the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_3(q), with \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1 and h = q - q^{-1}, let charge conjugation C\colon \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} act on braid words and let the bar involution \mathrm{bar}\colon q \mapsto q^{-1} act on coefficients. For the two-dimensional irreducible representation (2,1) and every braid word \beta \in B_3,

  \chi^{(2,1)}\bigl(C(\beta)\bigr)(q) = \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta)(q^{-1}).

The same identity holds for the one-dimensional characters of H_n(q) for every n, since these send \sigma_i to q or to -q^{-1}. So C = \mathrm{bar} holds on every irreducible character of H_3(q), not only on the one-dimensional ones.
prf:c-equals-bar-iff-all-1dim:
Proof Proof that charge conjugation equals the bar involution on characters. One-dimensional characters. A one-dimensional character sends every \sigma_i to the same eigenvalue \epsilon, either q or -q^{-1}. Then \sigma_i^{-1} \mapsto \epsilon^{-1}, and \epsilon^{-1}(q) = \epsilon(q^{-1}) in both cases, since q^{-1} = q^{-1} and (-q^{-1})^{-1} = -q = -(q^{-1})^{-1}. So \chi(C\beta)(q) = \chi(\beta)(q^{-1}) for every word.

The representation (2,1) of H_3(q). Take

  \sigma_0 \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} -q^{-1} & q \\ 0 & q \end{pmatrix},\qquad
  \sigma_1 \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} q & 0 \\ q^{-1} & -q^{-1} \end{pmatrix},

which is q times the reduced Burau matrices at t = q^{-2}. Write \rho_q for this representation. The matrix P = \mathrm{diag}(1, q^2) satisfies

  P\,\rho_q(\sigma_i^{-1}) = \rho_{q^{-1}}(\sigma_i)\,P
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  P\,\rho_q(\sigma_i) = \rho_{q^{-1}}(\sigma_i^{-1})\,P

for i = 0, 1. By induction on the length of a word, P\,\rho_q(C\beta)\,P^{-1} = \rho_{q^{-1}}(\beta) for every braid word \beta, and taking traces gives the identity. \square

The (2,1) identity holds for every braid word over any field with q \ne 0.

Remark (extension to every n). The same identity holds for every irreducible character of H_n(q). Let K = \mathbb{Q}(q) and let \iota be the ring involution of H_n(q) that sends q \mapsto q^{-1} and \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}. It is well defined because inverting every letter preserves the braid relations, and the quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1 becomes \sigma_i^{-2} = -h\,\sigma_i^{-1} + 1, which is the same relation multiplied by \sigma_i^{-2}. For an irreducible representation \rho with character \chi^\lambda, set \rho'(x) = \overline{\rho(\iota(x))}, where the outer bar applies q \mapsto q^{-1} to each entry. The two semilinear twists cancel, so \rho' is a K-linear irreducible representation with character \overline{\chi^\lambda(\iota(x))}. At q = 1 both twists are the identity, so \rho' and \rho specialise to the same irreducible character of S_n, and by Tits deformation \rho' \cong \rho. Evaluating on a braid word and barring both sides gives \chi^\lambda(C\beta)(q) = \chi^\lambda(\beta)(q^{-1}). Because Tits's deformation theorem is invoked externally for general n, the proposition above is stated explicitly for H_3(q).

Consequence for the meson word. On the meson word in H_3(q), the character \chi^{(2,1)} takes the exact value -(q^4 - q^2 + 1)/q^2 for the word, its charge conjugate, and its bar image alike. The character identity C = \mathrm{bar} therefore holds on (2,1) as well as on the one-dimensional characters: it does not single out H_2(q), and it does not separate a lepton level from a meson level.
def:spin-involution:
Definition Spin involution on a Frobenius *-algebra. Let (A, \tau, {}^*) be a Frobenius *-algebra over a commutative ring R. A spin involution on (A, \tau, {}^*) is an R-linear map \sigma : A \to A satisfying:

  1. Involution: \sigma \circ \sigma = \mathrm{id}_A.
  2. Anti-multiplicative: \sigma(a b) = \sigma(b)\, \sigma(a) for all a, b \in A.
  3. Trace-invariant: \tau \circ \sigma = \tau.
  4. *-compatible: \sigma(a^*) = \sigma(a)^* for all a.

The \mathbb{Z}/2 grading A = A_+ \oplus A_- by \sigma-eigenvalue defines the spin grading. The space A_+ is the spin-singlet sector and A_- is the spin-doublet sector.

When applying the A_\pm projections, assume 2 \in R^\times. Without this hypothesis, the projections a_\pm := \tfrac{1}{2}(a \pm \sigma(a)) are ill-defined.
rem:spin-involution-isospin:
Remark Isospin from the spin grading. Under a spin involution, every a \in A has the canonical decomposition a = a_+ + a_-. The isospin third-component evaluates on \sigma-eigenvectors as:

  T_3(a) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{sgn}_\sigma(a)
  \;\in\; \{-\tfrac{1}{2},\, 0,\, +\tfrac{1}{2}\}.

For a general a \in A, read T_3 off the A_\pm-projection a = a_+ + a_-. The derived spin grading secures the additive homomorphism properties, the orthogonality of the sectors A_+ \cap A_- = 0, and the explicit mapping 2\,T_3 = \mathrm{sgn}_\sigma.
prop:electroweak-triplet-bring-embedding:
Proposition The even-twist triplet T(2,4), T(2,6), T(2,8) co-embeds in Bring's genus-4 fiber. The even-twist 2-component torus links T(2,4), T(2,6), T(2,8) — the braids \sigma_1^{2k} \in B_2 for k = 2, 3, 4 — have Seifert genera 1, 2, 3 respectively. These genera strictly increase and satisfy g \leq 4 = g(\Sigma_4). The three links therefore co-embed in the genus-4 Seifert fiber of Bring's surface alongside the saturating force-carriers \{T(2,9), T(3,5)\}. Moreover, the three cells carry the pairwise-orthogonal Hoefsmit idempotent decomposition in \mathrm{End}_R(V^{\otimes 6}).

Proof.

The canonical Seifert surface of the 2-component torus link T(2, 2k) has genus g(T(2, 2k)) = k - 1. At k = 2, 3, 4 the genera are 1, 2, 3. These strictly increase and remain \leq 4. The even-twist links with genus in \{1, 2, 3\} are exactly those with k \in \{2, 3, 4\}. The embeddability bound g(K) \leq g(\Sigma_4) = 4 places all three in the same genus-4 Seifert fiber alongside the saturating carriers.

The genus, enumeration, and embedding steps involve elementary \mathbb{N}-arithmetic. The Hoefsmit idempotent orthogonality is cited from the prior theorem. \square

Scope. This proposition supplies the structural half of the electroweak torus-link story. It establishes that the triplet fits the genus-4 host. It does not fix which link carries W^\pm versus Z versus H. That physical identification constitutes the subsequent conjecture. This conjecture relies on the open selection, charge, and spin sub-conjectures.
thm:ew-triplet-far-commuting-minimal:
Theorem Far-commuting minimality: three even-twist torus-link generators fit minimally in B_6 at (1,3,5), enumerating \{T(2,4),T(2,6),T(2,8)\}. Let \sigma_a, \sigma_b, \sigma_c be pairwise far-commuting braid generators: |a-b|, |b-c|, |a-c| \geq 2. Then:

  1. (Minimality.) These generators require at least 6 strands: with 1 \leq a < b < c, the pairwise gap \geq 2 forces c \geq 5, hence
  n \geq c + 1 \geq 6, \qquad \text{attained uniquely by } (a,b,c) = (1,3,5) \in B_6 .
  1. (Enumeration.) The even-twist 2-component torus links T(2,2k) (braid \sigma_1^{2k}, Seifert genus g = k-1) with genus strictly between the trivial Hopf endpoint g=0 and the genus-4 Bring saturation (1 \leq g \leq 3) are exactly those with k \in \{2,3,4\}: the triplet T(2,4), T(2,6), T(2,8).

This forms the mathematical core of the electroweak selection principle. Both halves rely on elementary \mathbb{N}-arithmetic.
prf:ew-triplet-far-commuting-minimal:
Proof Far-commuting minimality and even-twist enumeration.

Far-commuting minimality

Each even-twist carrier T(2,2k) acts on a single strand-pair. Three mutually non-interfering carriers require three generators \sigma_a, \sigma_b, \sigma_c that pairwise commute without sharing a strand. This is the far-commutativity condition |i-j| \geq 2. In B_n, a generator \sigma_i requires 1 \leq i \leq n-1. Three indices with a \geq 1, b \geq a+2, c \geq b+2 dictate c \geq 5, so n = c+1 \geq 6. Setting c = 5 forces (a,b,c) = (1,3,5). The n=6 minimum supplies three disjoint strand-pairs \{1,2\}, \{3,4\}, \{5,6\} carrying \sigma_1^4, \sigma_3^6, \sigma_5^8.

Enumeration

The genus filtration places the trivial Hopf link T(2,2) at g=0 and the force-carrier saturation \{T(2,9), T(3,5)\} at g=4 = g(\Sigma_4). The open window 0 < g < 4 contains exactly the genera 1,2,3 (k \in \{2,3,4\}).
